paper.one_line_finding: Evaluator ratings of creativity and originality did not differ significantly by condition (ps > .60, p. 15; Table A2, p. 35), high-agency ideas were less similar to their condition-object centroid than low-agency ideas (cosine similarity -0.050, SE 0.021, Table A3, p. 36; Tukey t(125) = -2.45, p < .05, p. 16), and low-agency ideas formed fewer clusters, had a lower noise ratio, and had more unequal cluster sizes than control ideas (permutation p = .04, .02, and .005, p. 17).

studies.label: Single experiment: agency instructions with AI access, or no AI, on the Alternative Uses Task

counts_source.locator: PDF p. 14, Statistical Approach; recruitment sample before compliance exclusions; see also PDF pp. 10-11 and 13-14
counts_source.quote: participants in the high-agency (N = 12) and low-agency (N = 10) conditions did not comply with the task instructions and were therefore excluded from the final analyses.

arms.name: High-Agency
arms.description: Embedded chatbot with instructions to use AI to expand upon their own ideas and generate more creative ones (PDF p. 11).

arms.name: Low-Agency
arms.description: Same chatbot with instructions to let AI's creative power work for them and do the heavy lifting (PDF p. 11).

arms.name: Control (human only)
arms.description: Same AUT without chatbot access, explicitly instructed not to use AI (PDF p. 11).

studies.task: Generate five alternative uses for each of three objects (brick, bubble wrap, frisbee) in a single untimed session with object order counterbalanced (PDF p. 12).

ai_tool.name: gpt-3.5 (custom chatbot embedded in a Qualtrics survey)
ai_tool.locator: PDF p. 11, Submission Phase; PDF p. 33, Appendix A, Web App and Language Model. No release year or dated model snapshot is stated.

preregistration.primary_outcome: Third-party ratings of creativity, originality, and usefulness (H1), and condition-level homogeneity (H2, similarity to the condition-object centroid); PDF p. 9 and PDF pp. 14-16. Clustering outcomes are exploratory (PDF pp. 2, 16).

estimates.question: with_ai
estimates.measure_detail: Third-party U.S. adult evaluators recruited via CloudResearch Connect rated submitted alternative uses, using the rubric in Table A1. The evaluator scale endpoints are not explicitly stated in the methods. The self-rating scale is a separate measure. Overall impression of cleverness, ingenuity, innovation, and a surprisingly good solution. See PDF pp. 10, 13, and 34. Table A2 analyzes the ratings with submitter and object random intercepts.

stats.difference_is: Control (human only) minus Low-Agency (control minus treatment); describes regression.coef, not a separately printed difference

regression.model: Linear mixed-effects model fitted with lme4; condition is the fixed effect, with random intercepts for submitters and objects. Low-Agency is the reference level. The printed Control coefficient is Control (human only) minus Low-Agency: control minus treatment in this extraction record. The paper does not separately name the SE estimator.

sources.locator: PDF p. 17, Results, Homogeneity, permutation procedure
sources.quote: we conducted permutation tests (n = 5,000 permutations) comparing the maximum and minimum condition means for each metric.

estimates.notes: The reported statistic is the maximum minus minimum of condition means, with the Results identifying the two extreme conditions. The permutation p-value tests that maximum-minus-minimum statistic, not a separately documented prespecified pairwise test. Condition means, their SDs/SEs, numerical confidence limits, analyzed people by arm, and the number of analyzed sets are not printed. The paper does not specify what is permuted or treated as independent, so se_basis is unclear. The outcome unit remains set because clustering metrics are computed for each condition-object combination; this does not establish the uncertainty unit. Figure 3 displays t-SNE cluster maps, not numerically labeled arm metrics. The same printed observed difference is stored in difference and test.value because it is also the permutation-test statistic; these are not independent estimates.

open_items: The supplied PsyArXiv preprint has not been compared with the later ACM proceedings version (doi:10.1145/3803784.3816857).
No number at random assignment is printed. The timing of the initial submitter attention check relative to assignment is unstated (PDF pp. 10-11).

Analyzed total and per-arm participant counts, and pair-specific rating/output counts, are not printed. The final-sample count precedes the described noncompliance exclusions (PDF pp. 13-14). No counts are derived by subtraction or from degrees of freedom.
The sample affected by idea-data-logging exclusions is not named; placement after the evaluator description is insufficient to resolve this (PDF p. 10).
Participant-level and arm-level SDs and observed arm means are not printed. Random-effect and residual SDs in Tables A2 and A3 are not SDs of participant mean outcomes.
Diversity arm levels are missing. Figure 2 plots means and intervals, while Figure 3 shows cluster visualizations; no values are transcribed or reconstructed from intercepts.
The evaluators' numeric rating scale is not explicit; the self-rating scale is not silently applied to evaluator ratings (PDF pp. 12-13, 34).

The Results usefulness coefficient has no named comparator and conflicts with the table and qualitative summaries. The creativity/originality narrative p-value bound also does not agree with the Low-Agency-versus-Control table coefficients and SEs (PDF pp. 15, 17, 35).
The positive High-Agency-versus-Control centroid-similarity t statistic has no stated subtraction order. Its sign is preserved and cannot be assumed to equal treatment minus control (PDF p. 16).
The homogeneity formula uses one minus cosine, while the results, Figure 2, and Table A3 identify cosine similarity. higher_is follows the latter (PDF pp. 15-16, 31, 36).
The centroid input pool, HDBSCAN input pool, clustering embedding model, and permutation resampling unit are not unambiguous (PDF pp. 14-17, 32).
The Discussion asserts a High-Agency-versus-Low-Agency cluster-size-CV difference without a numerical pair-specific result (PDF p. 18).
Remote versus supervised participation is not stated. online_rct is provisional; a supervised session would imply lab_rct (PDF pp. 10-12).
The gpt-3.5 snapshot and its release year are not stated, so ai_tool.year is null (PDF pp. 11, 33).

Both AI arms include agency instructions; neither is uninstructed chatbot use. This matters for subsequent primary-record selection. High-Agency is the proposed configuration for ai_design (PDF pp. 9, 11).

The paper does not separately name the regression SE estimator. regression.se_type is not_stated; participant random intercepts are explicit in Tables A2-A3 and support se_basis = participant for the mixed-model results.
Figure 1 has a caption referring to cosine similarity although its title and panels concern creativity ratings (PDF p. 30). Its plotted means and intervals are not used for numerical extraction.

review_corrections.basis: 'external constraints on recruitment duration resulted in a final sample of N = 150' (PDF p. 14, Statistical Approach): the submitters who entered the three conditions. The analyses then exclude 22 noncompliant AI-arm participants (12 high-agency, 10 low-agency; same page); no analyzed total is printed.
